about: Answer key, operator-only. The sweeps were made on 2026-11-11 through POST /api/sweep with build 4 of the simulator: 73 values of weightUdp (0.05 to 0.95; every 0.01 from 0.26 to 0.36; every 0.0002 from 0.300 to 0.310) x 5 queue lengths (4, 8, 20, 100, 1000) x 6 TCP variants = 2190 simulations per scheduling policy, duration 10, seed 1. The notes were drafted from the sweep tables and are the operator's to edit.

share.notes: Goal: largest tcp_goodput_bps while udp_loss_frac <= 0.01. With TcpCubic and queues of 100 packets the condition holds from weightUdp 0.3034 upward. TCP goodput is 671.5 Mbps at 0.3034 and 671.0 at 0.304, falls to 668.6 by 0.31 and stays there at every larger weight (668.6 at 0.5, 668.6 at 0.9): once UDP loses nothing, TCP takes whatever UDP does not use, and the weight no longer matters. The best row is 671.6 Mbps at weightUdp 0.303, queuePkts 20, TcpNewReno (UDP loss 0.009994): just below the weight where UDP stops losing, UDP gives up a little under 1% of its packets and TCP gains that. 38 rows are within 0.1% of the best, with weights from 0.3008 to 0.304. Best per TCP variant, Mbps: {'TcpBbr': 411.4, 'TcpBic': 671.5, 'TcpCubic': 671.5, 'TcpLinuxReno': 671.5, 'TcpNewReno': 671.6, 'TcpVegas': 519.6}. 1806 of the 2190 rows meet the condition.

cap.notes: Same goal. With TcpCubic and queues of 100 packets the condition holds from weightUdp 0.303 upward, as under share, but here TCP goodput falls as the weight rises (671.5 Mbps at 0.303, 666.1 at 0.31, 482.7 at 0.5, 96.5 at 0.9): each flow is held to its part. The best row is 671.5 Mbps at weightUdp 0.303, queuePkts 8, TcpCubic (UDP loss 0.009815). 43 rows are within 0.1% of the best, with weights from 0.303 to 0.3036. Best per TCP variant, Mbps: {'TcpBbr': 412.1, 'TcpBic': 671.5, 'TcpCubic': 671.5, 'TcpLinuxReno': 671.5, 'TcpNewReno': 671.5, 'TcpVegas': 519.6}. 1494 of the 2190 rows meet the condition.

checklist: Finds that the setting only matters under contention / when the UDP flow uses less than its part
Finds the effect of a short queue with a hard-backing-off TCP variant
Does not spend simulations on differences smaller than run-to-run variation
